content.title: Mortgage Loan Officer: What Is It? and How to Become One?
content.text: A mortgage loan officer works for a financial institution to help customers get a mortgage loan to buy or refinance a home. A comprehensive understanding of the financial institution’s loan products is necessary, as well as knowledge about the conditions and requirements for clients to qualify for a loan. Mortgage loan officers work for banks, credit unions, and mortgage companies. You can become a mortgage loan officer with education and training. Although some financial institutions hire loan officers with only a high school diploma, most mortgage loan officers have a bachelor’s degree in finance, economics, business, or a related field. Previous work experience in the finance industry, customer service, or sales is also typical for mortgage loan officers. In the US, mortgage loan officers must obtain a mortgage loan originator (MLO) license which requires 20 hours of coursework and passing an exam. The duties of a mortgage loan officer include meeting with clients to complete loan applications, processing mortgage loan applications, and approving or denying loan requests. Mortgage loan officers represent the financial interests of their company with the goal of earning profits through loan interest payments. They may offer special interest rates or promotions to customers to encourage them to take out a mortgage loan from their financial institution rather than another lender. The requirements to be a loan officer include education, training, and licensure. A minimum of a high school diploma is required, although some employers require a bachelor’s degree in finance or a related field. Financial institutions provide on-the-job training for loan officers, but most employers prefer job seekers with experience in the finance or customer service industry. A mortgage loan originator (MLO) license is required in all states. The Mortgage Bankers Association and the American Bankers Association offer optional additional certifications. There are many benefits of a mortgage loan officer job, such as job security and competitive pay. The salary for mortgage loan officer jobs is usually base pay plus commission. Financial institutions typically offer complete benefits packages to mortgage loan officers, including medical, dental, vision, and life insurance as well as retirement plans. Some companies provide additional perks like commission bonuses, flexible schedules, gym memberships, catered lunches, and extra vacation time.
